disposition_reason: Modeled atmospheric selenium deposition to agricultural soils and projected declines; no measured food or human concentrations.

study.design: global aerosol-chemistry-climate modeling (SOCOL-AER) of sulfur and selenium deposition, 2005-2009 versus 2095-2099 under SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5, plus USA stream trend analysis

period.as_reported: 2005 to 2009 modeled; 2095 to 2099 projected; stream data 2000 to 2020

study.method: atmospheric model with selenium chemistry; emissions scaled from sulfur dioxide
study.qa: model compared with observed particulate selenium trends

non_numeric_findings: Projected end-of-century decline in selenium deposition to Northern Hemisphere agricultural soils of 55 to 80% (Abstract).
Agricultural soils in Asia, North America and Europe: selenium deposition decline 70 to 80% (SSP1-2.6) and 55 to 65% (SSP5-8.5); Africa, Australia and South America 3 to 25% (p. 3).
Global selenium deposition projected to fall 31% (SSP1-2.6) and 23% (SSP5-8.5) (p. 2).
Authors state known selenium resources could be exhausted within 40 years if 20 g Se per ha were applied to all wheat fields, citing earlier work (p. 4).
Sulfate and selenate compete for the same plant uptake pathway (p. 4).
